message.reasoning_content: Record description update. Key risks: polynomial accuracy for |x| up to 1.05 vs 1e-6 tolerance (minimax polynomial for asinh on [0,1.05]? note polynomial coeffs look like a degree-17 odd approx); for |x|>1.05 uses direct log formula in fp32 — catastrophic cancellation? Actually log(x+sqrt(1+x²)) is stable for large x, but near threshold fine. Risk: at x near 0, polynomial scaled by minimum... actually local_magnitude = min(magnitude, 1.05), clamped — but where selects so fine. Risk: polynomial accuracy at magnitude near 1.05 vs tolerance 1e-6 (coefficients truncated to ~9 digits, Horner fp32 rounding). Also sign handling: x<0 gives -absolute_value; x=+0 → where false → absolute_value = polynomial(0)=0 good; -0: x<0 false → absolute_value 0 → +0 (signed zeros equivalent per contract). Subnormals fine. Large x=65504: sqrt fine, log fp32 error? log of large argument relative error ~1e-7 → absolute error in asinh ~ log error; fp32 log relative error could exceed 1e-6 absolute? asinh(65504)≈11.79, fp32 log precision gives relative ~6e-8 → abs ~7e-7, ok-ish. Also enable_fp_fusion=false may matter.
